econometric_drivers.title: 100% Maritime Island Supply Logistics, Jones Act Clean Tanker Freights & DACO Price Regulation
econometric_drivers.description: Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands constitute the PADD 6 Caribbean petroleum district, an isolated island market completely decoupled from North American mainland pipeline infrastructure. Since the closure of the Caribbean Petroleum (CAPECO) Bayamón refinery in PR and Hovensa/Limetree Bay in St. Croix, 100% of refined motor fuel is imported via coastal product tankers. Under the Merchant Marine Act of 1920 (Jones Act), shipments from US Gulf Coast refining centers (Houston/Corpus Christi) must transit on Jones Act-qualified clean product tankers, adding a significant marine freight spread over Gulf Coast spot RBOB. Retail prices are monitored and surveyed daily in cents per liter (¢/L) by the Puerto Rico Department of Consumer Affairs (DACO), which enforces statutory profit margin caps and price freezes during declared states of emergency.
